text:
The scoreboard said seven, but the chances said closer to three and a half. St. Louis scored 7 on 3.44 expected goals, and a good share of the gap came from finishing on long odds: Adam Jiricek's snap shot in the third carried a 3% chance, as did Pius Suter's slap shot earlier in the period. Still, the Blues deserved to win 78% of the time in simulated replays of every shot, and they led in expected goals in all three periods, 1.31 to 0.52 in the first.

The game stayed tight on the scoresheet longer than the play suggested. Suter opened the scoring shorthanded at 14:28 of the first, and Jake Neighbours made it 2-0 in the second. Claude Giroux cut it to 2-1 with 2:08 left in the period, and Mason McTavish answered 33 seconds later on a backhand to restore the two-goal lead. Ottawa never got closer, and Samuel Ersson allowed 3.6 goals more than the shots he faced warranted.

The third period turned it into a rout. Suter's slap shot made it 4-1, Neighbours made it 5-1 at 14:46, McTavish scored on the power play at 15:33, and Jiricek followed at 16:32. McTavish finished with 2 goals and an assist, and the Blues generated 1.8 expected goals while he was on the ice against 0.09 allowed. Fabian Zetterlund added a power-play goal for Ottawa with 1:27 left. Joel Hofer faced 18 shots and stopped 16.
